ingredient: Sulfites / Sulfiting Agents (E220-228: Sodium/Potassium Bisulfite, Metabisulfite)
mechanism: Releases sulfur dioxide gas, which can trigger bronchoconstriction (wheezing, chest tightness) in an estimated 5-10% of people with asthma. Common in dried fruit, wine/beer, pickled foods, and processed shrimp.

restriction_rules.mechanism: Releases sulfur dioxide gas, which can trigger bronchoconstriction (wheezing, chest tightness) in an estimated 5-10% of people with asthma. Common in dried fruit, wine/beer, pickled foods, and processed shrimp.

ingredient: Soy Protein / Soy Isoflavones (concentrated form, e.g. supplements)
mechanism: Can inhibit thyroid peroxidase activity and, in concentrated amounts, may impair absorption of thyroid hormone replacement medication (e.g. levothyroxine); effect is more pronounced with low iodine intake.

restriction_rules.mechanism: Can inhibit thyroid peroxidase activity and, in concentrated amounts, may impair absorption of thyroid hormone replacement medication (e.g. levothyroxine); effect is more pronounced with low iodine intake.

mechanism: In celiac disease, gluten from wheat, barley, and rye triggers an immune-mediated intestinal injury. Management is a strict gluten-free diet; the 20-ppm value is a labeling standard, not a personal dose target.
source: Codex Alimentarius / FDA gluten-free standard (20 ppm), cross-checked

restriction_rules.tolerated_dose: Choose foods labeled gluten-free and avoid gluten-containing wheat, barley, and rye; the labeling standard is not a moderation target.
restriction_rules.danger_threshold: Presence of a gluten-containing wheat, barley, or rye ingredient, or an unresolved cross-contact concern.

mechanism: In a person with a confirmed peanut allergy, exposure can trigger an IgE-mediated allergic reaction, including anaphylaxis. Avoidance applies to oral exposure to the causative allergen.

restriction_rules.mechanism: Confirmed peanut allergy requires avoidance of peanut-containing foods and attention to allergen labeling/cross-contact risk.
